panels.description: Wide. The healer's low house from Chapter 4: packed-earth floor swept smooth, hearth smoke curling up to a hole in the thatch, slatted daylight. Nagoji sits propped against the wall on a woven mat, a clay bowl of rice gruel beside him; costume override: bare-chested, cream captivity dhoti, hair loose, hands in clean linen, the brand, a pale puckered patch of raised ridges blurred past reading, on the inner side of his LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, rope burns across his chest, faint chafe rings at the ankles, no irons. The healer (a woman in her fifties, plain cotton sari, grey-streaked hair) works at the hearth, half turned away. In the doorway, backlit by the bright coast: Ibrahim, shorter than the fishermen but broader; white turban; short grey-flecked beard with the scar cut through it as a bare pale line from his LEFT ear to the corner of his jaw; pale vest over a white mundu; no coat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The man they called *kapitan* introduced himself as Ibrahim.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had decided what kind of man I was before he opened his mouth.

panels.description: Two-shot. Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, pale vest) crouched on his heels at the edge of the mat, forearms on his knees, at eye level with Nagoji (bare-chested, bare-headed, clean chin, hair loose).

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You were on the Portuguese ship. The storm did not like her.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The storm did not like any of us. I took the chance it gave.

panels.description: Over Nagoji's LEFT shoulder: his branded left forearm in the near foreground, its inner side turned to camera, the pale ridged brand clear; one linen-wrapped hand resting on his knee at the frame edge. Ibrahim beyond (turban, grey-flecked beard), his eyeline locked on the brand: a horse trader looking over new stock.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You are Maratha.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You fought them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes.

panels.description: Tight on Ibrahim, three-quarter view with his LEFT cheek toward camera (screen right), so the scar reads on his ANATOMICAL LEFT, from the ear to the corner of the jaw, a bare pale line through the grey-flecked beard. White turban. His left thumb traces the scar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A habit, I would learn. It meant he was filing information away.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Our king fights them too. And their cousins, the Dutch.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: He will want to hear what you have seen.

panels.description: Ibrahim's thumb has stopped on the scar. His gaze slides off Nagoji toward the bright doorway and the sea beyond it. For one beat he is somewhere else, and his face is the largest thing in the panel. Nagoji in the soft foreground, bare-shouldered, watching him do it. Keep all lettering on Nagoji's side of the frame so the flicker reads without words.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The fishermen had spoken the name Travancore. I wanted to hear it from this man's mouth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Who is your king?

panels.description: Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard), still crouched on his heels at the mat's edge, eyes back on Nagoji, lips twitching toward a smile he does not allow.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You will learn his names and his titles in good time.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: For now, think of him as the man whose land you lie on. And whose patience with Europeans is thin.

panels.description: Ibrahim tips his head toward the healer without looking at her. She (fifties, plain cotton sari, grey-streaked hair) snorts, hands on her hips, a trace of betel red at the corner of her mouth. Nagoji on the mat between them.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: Can he travel?

copy.speaker: HEALER (Malayalam)
copy.text: He should rest another week, but you will not wait. Men like you never do.

panels.description: Ibrahim rising from his crouch, mild, already turning back to Nagoji on the mat.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: Men like me are paid to be impatient.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Can you ride in a cart, or on a horse?

panels.description: Full width. Nagoji's face (bare-headed, clean chin, hair loose). Nothing moves. Nothing at all. Bleeding into the panel edge like a stain, not a bordered flashback frame: the black mare's neck and mane from Chapter 1, a winter morning. A deliberate echo of Chapter 1, 6.5.
Nagoji pushing himself up the wall, one bandaged hand flat against it. Ibrahim already in the doorway, a turbaned silhouette against the light.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I can sit. I can walk, if there is no better way.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: There is a better way, though you will not like it.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Come.

panels.description: Wide. The fishing village at late afternoon, back in its habits: women drawing water at a well, children chasing each other, men patching nets in the shade of leaning palms. One net-mender glances down the path toward the sea. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard, pale vest) leads Nagoji inland, away from the shore. Nagoji now in the Chapter 5-6 costume: a loose, collarless cream homespun cotton tunic-shirt pulled on over the head, long sleeves, no buttons, no collar, no pocket, over a plain village cotton dhoti; the left sleeve down over the brand; hair tied back; bare-headed; barefoot; hands in clean linen.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The cloth smelled faintly of coconut smoke. After months of prison rags, it felt strange on my skin.

panels.description: A narrow track winding between flooded paddy plots. The water reflects the darkening sky in strips. The two men walk single file, small in the frame, Ibrahim's white turban leading. Nagoji's head is turned, catching a scent on the breeze.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Pepper.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: It sits in the lungs. It pays for guns.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji, eyes half closed, breathing it in. Behind him, at the paddy's edge, dark pepper vines climb the trunk of a support tree.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: On the Deccan we had fought for the routes that carried this smell north.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now I was at the source.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (off)
copy.text: And for kings. That too.

panels.description: A small clearing. An open two-wheeled wooden cart with spoked wooden wheels and no hood, two bullocks yoked to it; the carter (thin young man, bare-chested, short plain mundu, small topknot, clean-shaven, a goad stick) waits at the yoke. The cart bed is lined with sacks of plain coarse cloth and woven palm leaf, with no markings of any kind; one sack's mouth is open on dried, wrinkled black berries. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard) rests a hand on the load. Nagoji at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: We send word ahead. Our people are the vines that run along this coast.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: We carry news as well as goods.

panels.description: Nagoji in the foreground, level, watching him. Ibrahim beyond, half turned to the bullocks, his turban and beard catching the late light.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What do you tell them?

panels.description: Ibrahim's shrug, a little too careful, with a sidelong glance at Nagoji. Ibrahim: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, pale vest.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: That I found a branded Maratha officer on our beach. That he still has both eyes and more teeth than one would expect from the Viceroy's dungeons.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: That he speaks like a man who has led horse into gunfire and lived.

panels.description: Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard) up on the cart now, looking down, his broad hand held out. In the near foreground, Nagoji's linen-wrapped hand closing on it.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: A man like that has value.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The question is always to whom.

panels.description: Wide. Dusk, the sky shifting from bruised grey to deep blue. The cart is small on a broader road, the bullocks plodding, the carter walking at the yoke, Nagoji and Ibrahim on the sacks. Fireflies spark over the wet fields. Far off, a Kerala temple: low, tiered, sloping tiled roof with gables, a brass lamp-post before it; no tower.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (small)
copy.text: Rest. The road is long, and the bulls do not hurry.

panels.description: Two-shot on the sacks in the last blue light. Nagoji (bare-headed, clean chin, cream tunic-shirt) at screen left, his bandaged hands resting on his knees. Ibrahim at screen right facing him, so his LEFT cheek and the scar face the camera (white turban, grey-flecked beard).

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Your people. What do they think of this coast?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They think of it when they want money.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We have learned to ride down toward the ports, strike at caravans and warehouses, ride back before your masters answer.

panels.description: Closer, same axis. Ibrahim's head tilted, his left thumb resting on the scar. Nagoji meeting his look, flat and even.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Your masters. Not you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I serve, as all men serve. But I know the difference between a fort built to defend a people and a fort built to protect a treasury.

panels.description: Ibrahim alone in profile facing screen left, so his LEFT cheek and the scar face the camera: white turban and grey-flecked beard dark against the last of the deep blue sky, considering. Behind him, a small oil lantern hangs from the cart's front rail, just lit. It stays lit and is the warm key light from here to 6.1.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Our fortresses are both. You will see.

panels.description: A small settlement at dusk, lamps lit in doorways, the cart's lantern swinging. A knot of village boys runs alongside the cart, one of them pointing at Nagoji on the sacks. Nagoji looks back at them. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard) calls over his shoulder.

copy.speaker: BOY (Malayalam)
copy.text: Who is he?

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: A man who thought he could drown, then changed his mind.

panels.description: A wayside shrine by the road: a worn stone image under a tree hung with cloth strips and bangles, a small oil lamp burning before it. Ibrahim, down from the cart, offers a coin; an old woman in a plain white cotton wrap marks his forehead with ash. Her eyes have already gone past him to Nagoji on the cart, lit by its lantern.

copy.speaker: OLD WOMAN (Malayalam)
copy.text: That one carries storms in his bones.

panels.description: Nagoji with one eyebrow raised. Ibrahim climbing back up beside him, shrugging, a faint smear of ash now on his forehead below the white turban.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: I told her you carry horses there too.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Storms and horses can both be useful, if you know how to ride them.

panels.description: Wide, the largest panel on the page. The road climbs. The coconut palms have thinned; taller, denser trees with dark leaves close overhead, and low mist lies between the trunks. The cart is small under the canopy, its lantern the only warm light, Nagoji and Ibrahim (turban, faint ash) on the sacks. At the tree line, half in shadow, a single watcher: a Nair man, bare-chested, white mundu hitched to the knee, dark sash, hair in a topknot, spear upright, small round shield; no turban, no coat. He does not move.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Beyond these hills, the land belongs to men who answer only to the king. They do not like uninvited guests.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And with you?

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: With me you are still an uninvited guest. But one whose arrival has been announced.

panels.description: Wide. Evening deepening. A settlement larger than the fishing village, not yet a town: a small bazaar at a crossroads, stalls of spices, cloth, oil and trinkets under oil lamps, deep wheel ruts in packed earth. At its centre, a compound wall of red stone blocks broken by a wooden gate. The cart comes in, lantern swinging, the carter at the yoke, Nagoji and Ibrahim on the sacks. Two gate guards lounging there straighten: Nair men in short white cotton jackets, white mundus hitched to the knee, dark sashes, topknots, spears and small round shields; no turbans.

copy.speaker: GUARD (Malayalam)
copy.text: You come late, *kapitan*.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: The sea does not consult my schedule.

panels.description: At the gate. Nagoji still seated on the sacks. A guard peering up at him, his gaze on the bandaged hands and the line of the shoulders. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard, faint ash), standing by the wheel, jerks his chin toward Nagoji.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: This is the man I sent word about.

copy.speaker: GUARD (Malayalam)
copy.text: He looks like he should already be dead.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: He disagrees. Our king might too.

panels.description: Wide interior. A low hall, wooden pillars carved with curling designs, lamps hanging on chains, a packed-earth floor. Men sit cross-legged around a central mat: bare-chested, white mundus, some with shoulder cloths, hair in topknots. At the far end, on a slightly raised platform, the official with a stack of palm-leaf records and a stylus: older and heavier, a patient round face, bare-headed with a Kerala topknot, clean chin, greying moustache, bare torso, white mundu and a plain shoulder cloth; no crown, no turban, no beard, no sacred thread, no forehead marks. Every man in the room is angled toward him. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard, faint ash) leans to Nagoji's ear as they approach.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (whisper)
copy.text: This is not the king. He is busy elsewhere.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (whisper)
copy.text: This is one of his hands on this coast.

panels.description: Over the shoulders of Ibrahim (white turban) and Nagoji (bare head, hair tied back): the official on his platform looking up from his leaf, dry amusement in his round face (topknot, greying moustache, clean chin).

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: You bring me shipwreck.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (Malayalam)
copy.text: The sea brought him. I only stopped the crabs from finishing.

panels.description: Tight on the official, stylus poised above the leaf, his eyes on the stranger standing before him.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: Name.

panels.description: Nagoji standing at the edge of the mat, upright despite everything, answering the platform. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard, faint ash) a half step behind at his shoulder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In Goa they had written me down as a number.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Nagoji Sawant.

panels.description: Insert, tight, a deliberate echo of the ledger insert in Chapter 1: the official's stylus cutting strokes into the palm leaf. Marks only, no legible script.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (off, Malayalam)
copy.text: Service?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: *Huzurat* cavalry. Household horse under Chimaji Appa. Until the Portuguese netted me.

panels.description: Over the official's shoulder, looking down from the platform: his eyeline rests on Nagoji's LEFT sleeve, over the brand. Nagoji's bandaged hands are in the frame, held before him.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: You raided them?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: You know their forts?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Some.

panels.description: The official seated and raised on his platform at screen right, tapping the edge of his palm leaf with the stylus. At screen left, below him, Nagoji standing, and Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, faint ash) at Nagoji's shoulder, echoing the words low in Konkani.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: Our king sharpens his sword for the Dutch now. And for those local chiefs who think they can hide behind European flags.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: He has horse from Madurai, musketeers of his own, ships that slip between the foreign hulls at night.

panels.description: Close on the official, patient, waiting, the stylus still. Set the caption at the top of the panel; the question is the last thing lettered on the page.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Then came the question that would decide whether I was given a place in this new game, or quietly dropped into some ditch.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: What does a Maratha rider know that he does not already have?

panels.description: Reverse wide from behind the official's platform, looking down the hall: the official's bare shoulder, topknot and palm leaves dark in the near foreground; beyond, the seated men turned on their mats toward Nagoji, who stands small and upright at the edge of the central mat. Ibrahim (turban, grey-flecked beard, faint ash) at his shoulder, leaning in to translate. Nagoji's eyes are not on Ibrahim; they are on the official. Rafters and hanging lamps above leave room for the balloons.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Your king knows his own land. He knows these hills, these backwaters, which chiefs will bend and which must be broken.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The Dutch and the Portuguese know their books and their drills.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know how men like them think when they stand on foreign soil and believe God and powder have made them superior.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's eyes, flat and certain.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know what a horse can do to a musket line when the man in the saddle has stopped being impressed by white skin.

panels.description: Narrow, side-on across the hall. Silence. The seated men motionless. The official's stylus lifted off the leaf; at the corner of his mouth, the slight smile just starting.

The official in the mid-ground at a readable size, on his platform, the slight smile, the stylus resting. Nagoji in the foreground, lowering his head in a measured bow, not deep. Ibrahim (turban, faint ash) a step behind him. The official's balloons sit high beside the official; the captions sit in the foreground space around Nagoji's lowered head.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: You speak well for someone who almost fed the fish.

copy.speaker: OFFICIAL (Malayalam)
copy.text: Tomorrow we take you to the king's war hall. He can decide whether your words are as sharp as you think.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not as a subject, not yet,

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: but as a man who understands that some battles begin with a lowered gaze and a measured tone.

panels.description: Full width, bottom, the tallest tier. Night, moonlight the only light. Camera slightly high inside the compound. In the lower foreground, Nagoji asleep on a mat under the eaves, one bandaged hand lying loosely curled on the mat, as if around reins. Beyond him the red stone wall, and over the top of it, pepper vines on their support trees and the pale road running away south into the dark. The captions sit in the moonlit sky.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere to the south a king I had not yet met considered maps covered in salt stains and ink.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The road that had begun in a Goan dungeon now pointed toward him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Horses. Guns. Storms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: When sleep came, it carried no dreams of drowning. Only the steady beat of hooves on sand, and a distant roar like the sea.
